proposals.evidence: DEDR 23 full article: Ka. akka ( nom. sg. akkaṃ , i.e. akkan, nom. pl. akkaṅgaḷ/akkandir ) elder sister; a woman older than oneself is usually termed akka , endearingly girls are also so called by their elders. Koḍ. akkë elder… Kannada akka is “elder sister”; the merged elder/younger Census gloss is narrowed to its elder sense.

proposals.evidence: DEDR 2591 full article: Ka. eṟake, eṟaṅke, ṟakke, ṟekke wing; ṟaṭṭe, ṟeṭṭe wing, upper arm. Koḍ. rekke wing; raṭṭe upper arm. Tu. ediṅke, reṅkè wing. Te. eṟaka, ṟekka, rekka, neṟaka, neṟi id. Kol. reḍapa, (SR.) reppā id.; (P.) reṛapa… The article includes Kannada ṟekke and Kodagu rekke “wing,” with related feather reflexes; the Census uses rekka for feather.
